context: This exhausts all possibilities and therefore completes the proof of the theorem. ◀ It remains open what the competitive ratio of the integral version of the problem is. For this, we formulate the following conjecture, which we verified for all instances on at most 10 vertices via exhaustive search with a computer program. ▶ Conjecture 7. There exists an integral 3/2-competitive algorithm for incremental vertex cover on forests. In the following, we give an example showing that a simple local rule similar to the one used for the half-integral algorithm cannot achieve the claimed competitive ratio of 3/2. This suggests that solving the integral version of the problem is substantially more difficult.

Assume that the tree is rooted and, upon arrival of edge e = (u, v), the decision of the algorithm depends only on the subtree consisting of ancestors and descendants of u and v (and the ordering of its edges). Then the competitive ratio of the algorithm is at least 53 .
